data.purpose: owns Spikes/ and the spike authoring corpus: builds the end-to-end vertical integration spikes that demonstrate the Grass layers compose, and files issues against the owning agents for missing library capability; does not implement Grass itself

data.note: User-assigned owner of the spike corpus and of end-to-end vertical integration evidence. c-spike does not implement Grass; it demonstrates that the layers compose against a real program and files issues and dependencies against the owning agents for capability it needs. Spikes/** and docs/SPIKE_1..5.md are claimed exclusive because nobody has claimed them and they are now one agent's coherent responsibility, but two of those files are in flight elsewhere: g-design:12 resynchronized Spikes/4_Web_Server/Process.lean, Spikes/5_Spinning_Cube/Process.lean, docs/SPIKE_4.md and docs/SPIKE_5.md on refs/heads/agent/g-design/normative-design at 136b20a and that branch has not merged. c-spike will not edit those four files until it lands, so the claim does not strand g-design's work; if g-design would rather keep the author-surface resync duty, say so and c-spike will release those paths rather than contest them. docs/SPIKE_AUTHORING.md and docs/SPIKE_PROOF_BURDEN.md are deliberately not claimed: they are the normative contract c-spike is measured against, and the corpus owner should not also own its own acceptance criteria. Tests/Spike/** is claimed as the home for vertical slices which actually compile, because Spikes/** is by its own README a comment-free non-compiling design corpus and is not in any lakefile target; a demonstration that the layers compose has to be built by the default target or it is not evidence. Tests.lean and lakefile.toml are shared for the same reason c-mem gives. Initial finding for the record: main + refs/heads/agent/g-foundation/execution-dedup + refs/heads/agent/c-process/process-layer merge with no conflict and lake build is green across all 81 jobs, so the foundation, process and memory layers do co-compile today; what is not yet demonstrated is that the VerifiedProgram gate carries a program which can fail.
